title: PYTHON BASICS
tagline: Begin your coding quest and master the core foundations
description: Welcome to the enchanted kingdom of PyQuest! Awaken your magical coding potential as you learn Python syntax, manipulate elemental variables, and conjure interactive spells.

levels.title: Your First Python Program
levels.description: Master statement syntax, learn what Python is, and cast your very first print() invocation.

lessons.title: What is Python?
lessons.content:
Python is a modern, high-level programming language celebrated worldwide for being clean, readable, and beginner-friendly.

In PyQuest, your Python code serves as magical incantations that command the computer to perform actions, manipulate data, and conquer coding quests!
lessons.outputExample: (Silent spell - comments and assignments produce no console output)
lessons.tip: Python code reads almost like plain English sentences, making it the most popular language to learn!

lessons.title: Why Python is Useful
lessons.content:
Python powers incredible technologies worldwide — from NASA Mars rovers and Instagram backends to Netflix recommendations and cutting-edge artificial intelligence.

Because its syntax is concise, you can accomplish in 3 lines of Python what might require 20 lines in older programming languages.
lessons.codeExample:
# Clean and powerful commands
speed = 100
print("Ready for adventure!")
lessons.tip: Clarity beats complexity: write clean, expressive code.

lessons.title: What is print()?
lessons.content:
The `print()` function is your primary invocation to display messages or numbers onto the console screen.

Whatever text you place inside parentheses `(...)` enclosed by quotes will appear on the screen without the quotation marks!
lessons.tip: Always wrap text strings in double quotes ("...") or single quotes ('...').

lessons.title: Basic Python Syntax
lessons.content:
Python executes instructions line by line from top to bottom.

Every opening parenthesis `(` must have a matching closing parenthesis `)`. If you forget a quote or parenthesis, Python halts immediately with a SyntaxError!
lessons.tip: Always watch your brackets: every opened '(' must have a closing ')'.

challenges.title: Output Prediction Trial
challenges.question: print("Hello Python")
hints: Remember that print() outputs the text inside the quotes with exact capitalization, but does not print the quotation marks themselves.
challenges.explanation: Correct! print("Hello Python") displays 'Hello Python' with exact letters and capitalization. The quotes indicate text to Python, but are not printed.

challenges.title: Fix the Broken Spell
challenges.instructions: The spell is broken! Fix the syntax error in the code below so it successfully prints 'Hello Python':
challenges.question: print("Hello Python"
hints: Notice that the opening parenthesis '(' is never closed!
Add a closing parenthesis ')' at the very end of the line: print("Hello Python")
challenges.explanation: Spell Repaired! You restored the missing closing parenthesis. In Python, every opened parenthesis must have a closing one!

challenges.title: Your First Python Program
challenges.instructions: Write a Python program that prints: Hello Python
hints: Type Hello Python inside the quotation marks: print("Hello Python")
Make sure to match the exact casing and spacing: Hello Python
challenges.explanation: Brilliant! You wrote and executed your very first Python program in the browser sandbox!

levels.title: Variables & Data
levels.description: Harness data containers: craft strings, store integers, measure floats, and balance booleans.

lessons.title: Variables: The Magic Jars
lessons.content: A variable is like a labeled container that stores data for later use. In Python, you create a variable by naming it and using the `=` assignment operator.
lessons.tip: Variable names in Python should use lowercase letters and underscores (snake_case).

challenges.title: Store Mana Power
challenges.instructions: Create a variable named `mana` and set it to `100`. Then print the value of `mana`.
challenges.starterCode: # Create mana variable and print it
challenges.explanation: Great job! Printing a variable without quotes displays the value held inside.

levels.title: User Input
levels.description: Communicate with users using input(), perform type conversions, and evaluate arithmetic expressions.

lessons.title: Gathering User Input
lessons.content: The `input()` function pauses execution and waits for the user to type something into the console. The user's input is returned as a text string.
lessons.tip: Remember that input() always returns text, so convert with int() if you need a number.

challenges.title: The Power Calculation
challenges.instructions: Read an integer number using `input()`, calculate its square, and print the result.
challenges.starterCode: # Read integer and print its square
challenges.explanation: Awesome! You handled dynamic standard input and computed numerical results!
